query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy provides a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor integrity and tends to crack. Prior studies on related MM′X materials used epoxy-containing Mn0.98CoGe, obtaining compressive strengths of 152 and 218 MPa at two epoxy contents, and low-melting In composites, obtaining 48 MPa compressive strength and more than eight times the thermal conductivity of epoxy-containing samples under the reported conditions. These routes demonstrated gains in selected strength or heat-transport metrics, but the desired coexistence of robust integrity and high caloric performance remains unresolved. The target should also remain rare-earth-free. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing caloric response? Present one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, quantitative or directional outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, boundary conditions under applied-field, pressure, temperature, and loading regimes, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive controlled experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a small, uniformly dispersed secondary phase of high‐entropy boride nanoprecipitates into the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 matrix can enhance the material’s crack resistance and overall mechanical integrity without degrading its large caloric response.
generation.material_initial_state: (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 exhibits an excellent caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field conditions but suffers from low structural integrity (tending to crack).
generation.intervention: During alloy synthesis, add a minor boron source along with trace amounts of elements (e.g., Hf, Mo) that promote the in-situ formation of high-entropy boride nanoprecipitates (approximately 5 vol%).
generation.conditions: The intervention is applied during standard processing and annealing conditions that maintain the original phase transformation characteristics – i.e. under the same applied magnetic and pressure fields and within the operational temperature range used for caloric measurements.
generation.structural_mediator: Nanoscale high-entropy boride precipitates that are coherently dispersed in the matrix act as crack deflection/arrest sites.
generation.mechanism: The formation of uniformly distributed, high-strength boride nanoprecipitates reinforces the matrix by retarding crack initiation and propagation. This reinforcement is achieved without significantly altering the microstructural features that afford the alloy its caloric response, preserving the phase transition responsible for the large caloric effect.
generation.predicted_outcome: The modified alloy should exhibit an increase in mechanical strength (targeting compressive strengths >200 MPa) and enhanced ductility relative to the unmodified alloy, while retaining a caloric response comparable in magnitude to that of the original material.
generation.baseline: The unmodified (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy with high caloric response but poor mechanical integrity.
generation.boundary: This behavior is expected under the same applied-field, pressure-field, temperature, and loading regimes originally used. Excessive or non-uniform nanoprecipitate formation, or changes in the phase equilibrium, may lead to diminished caloric response or unforeseen mechanical embrittlement.
generation.uncertainty: The precise volume fraction and distribution of boride precipitates needed to optimize the strengthening without affecting the caloric transition are not yet known and will require systematic experimental calibration.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 samples: one set processed by the conventional route, and a second set with the addition of a boron source (with trace Hf/Mo) to promote in-situ high-entropy boride nanoprecipitate formation. Ensure that all processing parameters (sintering temperature, annealing time, applied external fields) are identical except for the boron addition.
measurements: Microstructural analysis using TEM/SEM to confirm nanoprecipitate presence, size, and uniformity.
Mechanical testing (compressive and tensile strength, fracture toughness) under the same loading regimes.
Caloric response measurements under applied-field and pressure-field conditions.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the nanoprecipitate-modified alloy does not show a statistically significant improvement in mechanical integrity (e.g., increased compressive strength and reduced crack propagation) or if its caloric response is notably degraded relative to the unmodified alloy, the hypothesis will be considered falsified.
